title.rendered: I Am Seated With Christ in Heavenly Places: The Gospel For Today

content.rendered:
God raised us up with Christ and seated us with Him in the heavenly realms in Christ Jesus. Past tense. Already done. The believer is not waiting to be seated. The believer is already there.

The Gospel For Today | Wednesday, July 1, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“And God raised us up with Christ and seated us with him in the heavenly realms in Christ Jesus.”
Ephesians 2:6 (NIV)

Today’s Message

Paul writes Ephesians from a Roman prison. He is physically chained to a wall. His freedom of movement is gone. His future is uncertain. And in chapter two, he tells the Ephesian believers something that should have stopped them in their tracks. They have been raised up with Christ. They have been seated with Him in heavenly places. The same Paul who is sitting on a stone floor in a Roman cell is writing that, in Christ, his position is in the heavenly realms.

The Greek verb Paul uses for “seated” is in the aorist tense, which means a completed past action. It is not “God is in the process of seating us.” It is “God has seated us.” The work has been done. The chair is occupied. The believer, by virtue of being in Christ, shares the position Christ holds at the right hand of the Father.

This is not abstract theology. It is the foundation of spiritual authority. When the believer prays, they pray not from earth toward heaven but from heaven into earth. When the believer faces an attack from the enemy, they face it not from beneath but from above. When the believer brings a problem to God, they do not approach as a stranger trying to get into the throne room. They are already seated in it. The work of every prayer life is learning to walk in the position the cross has already secured.

This is also what makes Paul’s letter from prison so striking. By any normal measure, Paul is in the worst possible position. By the measure of who he is in Christ, Paul is in the highest possible position. The Roman jailers do not see it. Paul himself, by faith, does. He writes from the heavenly realms while sitting in a Roman cell, and the letter has shaped two thousand years of Christian thinking about identity ever since.

For Gospelbuzz readers, the application today is simple. Whatever your physical circumstances are this morning, your spiritual position is already in Christ at the right hand of the Father. The cell you may feel you are sitting in is not the deepest truth about you. The throne where you are seated, in Christ, is. Walk in it today.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that I am seated with Christ in heavenly places. This is my position today, by Your grace and through the finished work of Jesus. I do not pray from beneath my problems. I pray from above them, in the place You have already given me to occupy. I face this day from the throne, not toward the throne. The authority that flows from this position is mine in Christ. I walk in it today, confidently and at home in heavenly places. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I am seated with Christ in heavenly places. My position is settled in Him. I face today from the throne, not toward it. The authority of Christ is the authority I walk in.
